title: The Structure
description: How The Labs is put together: who does what, how you're recognized, and how one city becomes a network. A working draft.
draft: Brendan's working draft, for the board. Nothing on this page is approved yet.

title: The
Structure
hero.lede: How The Labs is put together. Who does what, how you're recognized, and how one city becomes a network.

shape.title: One network. Many regions. Lots of neighborhoods.
shape.lede: Same shape as the YMCA: a national body, metro associations, and branches. Regions follow national on the standard and the brand, and run everything else themselves.

levels.label: National
levels.title: The Upskilling Labs
levels.body: Holds the commons: the playbooks, the platform, the standard, and the brand. Its board hires the CEO.

levels.label: Regional
levels.title: The Upskilling Labs of your region
levels.body: Its own board and its own director. Runs the programs, signs the venue deals, and keeps its own books. A team for each workstream runs across the whole region.

levels.label: Neighborhood
levels.title: Your local Lab
levels.body: A small committee with a few places, like a library branch. It brings the region's work to those places, and it's where new ideas get tried first.

work.title: Five kinds of work.
work.lede: Regional teams run each workstream across the region. Neighborhood committees bring them to their places. Together they make a grid.

items.title: Build Cycle
items.body: Small teams, which we call pods, build real things for real local problems over a few weeks, then show them at Demo Day.

items.title: Learning Pathways
items.body: Free workshops by Mentors, people who do the work, and by Upskillers who learned it last cycle.

items.title: Community & Outreach
items.body: Ambassadors, partners, and how new people find The Labs.

items.title: Platform
items.body: OLOS, the software The Labs runs on. Each region runs its own copy, kept close to the national one.

items.title: Operations & Governance
items.body: Money, venues, the register, and the boards.

work.note: The list is a draft. Founding new regions may become a sixth. [PLACEHOLDER]

roles.title: A button says what you're doing.
roles.lede: A role is a door into a workstream, and a workstream is much bigger than a role. Ambassador opens onto comms overall. Every role starts with training and a button. Practice it for real and the button gets a metal rim.

items.label: Upskiller
items.title: Anyone in a Build Cycle.
items.body: Practiced, you're a Builder: the Upskiller button with a brass rim, after a real contribution to a real problem.

items.label: Poderator
items.title: Runs a pod.
items.body: Comes after you've been through a cycle yourself. One per pod.

items.label: Mentor
items.title: Shares what they know.
items.body: The door into Learning Pathways: workshops, and helping pods. Everyone has something to teach.

items.label: Ambassador
items.title: Brings people in.
items.body: One conversation at a time. Open now.

members.title: Two ways to be a member. Take either, or both.

items.label: Supporting Member
items.title: You back it.
items.body: Chip in a little each year and wear the button that says so. Dues buy the button, never a pin, and never a vote.

items.label: Contributing Member
items.title: You built some of it.
items.body: Something you gave is now part of how The Labs runs. People who saw it put your name forward, and you wear the pin.

pin.title: Four levels. Each one puts more of The Labs in your hands.
pin.lede: The pin is trust, not a trophy: a say over your region's playbooks, tools, kits and platform. Brass for a region, silver for national. Yours forever. The seat takes showing up.

levels.title: Contributing Member
levels.body: The bare pin. One part of The Labs runs on something you gave.

levels.title: Reviewer
levels.body: One ring. Hands-on in two major workstreams, with two people who wear the pin vouching for you.

levels.title: Approver
levels.body: Two rings. Hands-on in every major workstream. Says yes to changes in the Lab's playbooks.

levels.title: Maintainer
levels.body: Three rings. Hands-on across the board. Put forward by the other Maintainers, confirmed by the board.

pin.link: The whole story, told to a person: the Contributor Community page

objects.title: Button, rim, pin, coin.

items.label: Button
items.title: What you're doing.
items.body: Given on training. Printed paper, so it's easy to reissue.

items.label: Rim
items.title: What you've practiced.
items.body: Real metal added to your own button. It moves to your next one.

items.label: Pin
items.title: What you've been trusted with.
items.body: Earned, numbered, and on the register. Merit pins are the orb. Office pins, for a seat on a committee or board, are a different shape.

items.label: Coin
items.title: A moment, or a thanks.
items.body: No status at all, so anyone can get one, even outside The Labs. A founding coin, a cycle coin, a leader's coin.

objects.note: The rule for a pin: it's given, never bought. It lasts. It's scarce. And it's on the register. Miss any one of those and it's a button.

decides.title: Levels recognize. Seats carry the say. Boards set the rules.
rules: Every level is active or emeritus. Active means a seat in your Lab and the say that comes with it. Step back and you keep the pin, the level, and your voice.
Seats are limited, follow the work, and are reconfirmed every Build Cycle. One Poderator per pod. At least two Approvers for every workstream, so nothing depends on one person.
The say is granted once, in writing, by the board to every active Approver at once. It lapses when you step back. The board can change it.
No level carries a vote. The boards look after programs, money, people and the brand.
Everything is written down in the register. The handshake is the ceremony. The register is the record.
The only way to lose a level is to seriously break the Code of Conduct.

starts.title: One city first. Then the next.

steps.title: One entity.
steps.body: Regions begin as steering committees inside The Labs. Greater Washington is first.

steps.title: The CEO runs DC, for now.
steps.body: They support the steering committee and hire one person to serve it directly.

steps.title: That person builds the network.
steps.body: Everything they do in DC gets written down as the launch kit. Then they help found the next region with it.

steps.title: DC spins off.
steps.body: When it runs a full cycle on its own, pays for its own staff, and has its own director lined up, it becomes The Upskilling Labs of Greater Washington.

grows.title: Try it in a neighborhood. Adopt it in the region. Send it upstream.
grows.lede: Playbooks and code move the same way, in three stages.

stages.label: Pilot
stages.title: A neighborhood Lab tries it.
stages.body: At its own places, with the region's workstream team.

stages.label: Regional
stages.title: The region adopts it.
stages.body: In its own copy of the platform and playbooks.

stages.label: National
stages.title: It goes into the standard.
stages.body: With a note on where it was tried and what happened.

grows.note: Regions keep their copy close to the national one, keep people's data local, and send only the numbers up. Anyone can use the open code and playbooks. Only a chartered region can call itself The Upskilling Labs of somewhere.

open.title: What the board still has to decide.
items: The workstreams, and the names of the levels.
The dues, and what a Supporting Member gets.
Exactly what an active Approver can do.
How many seats, how long a term, and how long before someone goes emeritus.
When Greater Washington is ready to spin off.
The neighborhood committee: its size, its term, and its pin.

join.title: Come build it.
join.lede: The Contributor Community page is this same system, told to a person. The ambassador program is the open door.
